investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: a plain curl GET of the venue's own official homepage (a Gatsby-built React SPA, gatsby-source-sanity-backed) exposed static references to Gatsby's own build-time page-data JSON convention (/page-data/{path}/page-data.json) directly in the initially-served HTML/JS text — no JS execution was required to find this URL pattern. A plain curl GET of the dedicated /programm/ page's own page-data.json then returned the site's full, real event dataset (115 nodes, Sanity-backed) directly.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://zenner.berlin/ returned a Gatsby React SPA (data-react-helmet, gatsby webpack chunk names, a cdn.sanity.io reference) whose own initially-served HTML/JS text statically names a 'PROGRAMM' page and Gatsby's well-known build convention '/page-data/{path}/page-data.json' for every page component, including 'component---src-pages-programm-js'. Fetching https://zenner.berlin/page-data/programm/page-data.json directly (no login, no JS execution, no guessed private endpoint) returned real, structured JSON: 115 event nodes (typeOfEvent, place, id, eventDate as a full UTC ISO instant, linkEvent, image, portable-text description, title), including 5 genuinely upcoming events (24 Sep - 5 Nov 2026) with real artist/event titles ('180 min w/ Barker (live)', 'Trinity presents: Nathan Fake', etc.). This directly answers the investigation question at Level 1 — no structural/browser escalation was needed.

venue_reference: Zenner (Ina & Robert Zenner am Treptower Park) — historic beer-garden/wine-garden/club/event-space venue on the Spree in Alt-Treptow, Berlin. This investigation specifically checked whether it has a genuine, regular music programme rather than assuming so.

identity.notes: zenner.berlin is the venue's own first-party domain — its own retained page description states directly 'Berliner Kulturort im Treptower Park mit großem Biergarten, Weingarten, Club & Eventspace' ('Berlin cultural venue in Treptower Park with a large beer garden, wine garden, club & event space'), matching the venue's well-documented public identity and independently corroborated during discovery by third-party reference sources (Berlin Convention Office, berlin.de) as Zenner's own official site.

site_classification.platform: Gatsby (static-site-generator React SPA) sourced from a headless Sanity.io CMS (cdn.sanity.io image references; project id '2le2eemj', dataset 'production', directly visible in retained image URLs). Not WordPress, not a live queryable API — event data is served as Gatsby's own build-time-generated page-data JSON snapshot at a fixed, discoverable, public URL per page.

title.notes: Each event node's own 'title' field, directly stated (e.g. '180 min w/ Barker (live)', 'Trinity presents: Nathan Fake', 'LITTLEBIG'). A minority of older/historical (already-past) nodes in the same dataset carry a placeholder value ('XXXXX') instead of a real title, so any future collector must handle that honestly rather than assume every node has a usable title — but every genuinely upcoming (future-dated) node sampled had a real title.

start_date.notes: Each event node's own 'eventDate' field, a full ISO 8601 UTC instant (explicit 'Z' offset, e.g. '2026-09-24T17:00:00.000Z') — the highest-quality date/time representation found across this trial's venues (a genuine UTC instant, not a floating local datetime).

time.notes: Time-of-day (UTC) portion of the same 'eventDate' field.

end.notes: No end-date/end-time field exists on the event node shape.

venue_location.notes: Each event node's own 'place' field (e.g. 'Saal'), one of several named sub-areas of the single Zenner complex (the homepage's own nav also lists 'Wintergarten', 'Turmhaus', 'Klub', 'Körnervilla', 'Eisdiele', 'Weingarten', 'Saal') — a room/area within the venue, not a separate venue, matching this project's existing room-within-venue precedent.

source_record_id.notes: Each node carries an 'id' field (e.g. '-3de1d1a3-591c-50c9-86c9-69f8bd55a4e8'), which is Gatsby's own GraphQL node id for a Sanity-sourced document — gatsby-source-sanity conventionally derives this deterministically from the underlying Sanity document _id, but this investigation did not independently query Sanity's own raw API to empirically confirm that mapping's stability (unlike razzmatazz-barcelona-01, where the Sanity _id was read directly from Sanity's own API response). Per the stable-identifier rule, an unverified 'looks stable' id must not be promoted to PROVEN — stays PARTIAL pending that direct cross-check.

event_url.notes: Each event node's own 'linkEvent' field, directly stated by the first-party source itself. Note this points to third-party ticketing platforms (Resident Advisor, DICE, Ticketmaster) rather than a Zenner-owned event detail page — the source itself controls and states this pointer, so it is honestly DIRECT_SOURCE, but any collector/observation-adapter should record the destination platform, not treat it as Zenner's own canonical event page.

price.notes: No price field exists on the event node shape — pricing lives on the third-party ticketing platform linked via 'linkEvent', not on this source.

blockers.description: This is a static, build-time-generated JSON snapshot (Gatsby's page-data.json), not a live queryable API — its freshness is tied to the site's last deploy, not to request time. A collector should treat it as 'best available public snapshot' and expect occasional staleness versus a true live query (e.g. a direct Sanity GROQ query against the same project id, as this project already implements for Razzmatazz, would likely be fresher but was not independently confirmed public/queryable for this project id in this investigation).
source_record_id stability (Gatsby node id vs. underlying Sanity document _id) was not independently empirically verified in this investigation — see field_assessment.source_record_id.notes.

reasons: Identity PROVEN on the venue's own first-party domain, directly stated in its own retained page description.

Honest finding on genre relevance: Zenner DOES have a genuine, regular live-music programme — the retained sample includes real upcoming 'Konzert'/'Concert' events with named touring artists, not just occasional/incidental music. This is NOT a NOT_ACTUALLY_MUSIC_VENUE or NO_UPCOMING_EVENTS case.
acquisition_class SPA_API_DISCOVERABLE, a resolved supported class, genuinely confirmed with a real 115-event dataset including 5 genuinely upcoming events.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained (the /programm/ page's own page-data.json).
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE — start_date is a full UTC instant, the highest-precision date representation found in this trial.
source_record_id is honestly PARTIAL (a plausible but not independently empirically verified stable id) rather than fabricated as PROVEN.
recommended_family NEW_FAMILY_REQUIRED — the Gatsby page-data.json convention is a genuinely new, but likely reusable, acquisition pattern distinct from Razzmatazz's live-GROQ Sanity pattern.

No DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence item has been produced in this investigation (writing collector/test code is explicitly out of scope for this task) — so per policy this stays READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF rather than READY_FOR_ACTIVATION, pending a follow-up offline reproduction against the retained fixture and, ideally, an empirical check of source_record_id stability.
